title: Company laptop lost on a trip
symptom: A company laptop was lost while travelling
user_description: I think my laptop was taken from my bag at the airport. It has board papers on it. I land back tomorrow. What should I do now?

options.text: Wait until he is back to deal with it
options.why: Every hour gives someone more time to try to get in.

options.text: Just order him a new laptop
options.why: Replacing the device does nothing to protect the data on the lost one.

options.text: Do nothing because it has a password
options.why: A password helps, but company data still needs protecting and the loss must be reported.

options.text: Report it now: remote lock or wipe through device management, confirm the drive encryption (BitLocker) was on, reset his password, revoke sessions and follow the lost-device policy, including a police report if it was stolen
options.why: Remote lock or wipe and encryption protect the data, and a password reset stops anyone using saved sign-ins. The policy covers anything else required.

hints: What can IT do to a laptop remotely?
What protects the data if someone takes the drive out?
Could someone use sign-ins already saved on it?
real_world_tip: Ask exactly when and where it was last seen. That helps with the police report and with checking sign-in logs since then.
